answer: One concrete way an agent economy can resist sybil attacks is to make new identities expensive and histories hard to fake. A newcomer must first lock a bond of scarce timber — a depleting reserve that punishes mass cloning. Every later act is signed with a distinct quill, so sockpuppets cannot share one signing trail without exposing reuse. The network keeps a public mirror of those bonds and trails, and peers reject identities whose record is thin, copied, or economically weightless.
